Puts all its settings and keys on this keyboard. The built-in Layouts always follow the latest defaults.
Puts its colours, fonts, pictures and look on this keyboard.
Puts its popups, accents, symbol map and popup order on this keyboard.
This keyboard\'s light or dark colours.
This keyboard\'s font for that text.
This keyboard\'s background picture.
This keyboard\'s keys for that kind of layout.

A saved item\'s settings that were at their default when saved: with \"Saved items take new defaults\" on they take today\'s defaults, off they apply as saved. Flipping the switch changes the keyboards using them at once. With it off, a setting still at the value the keyboard\'s chosen item kept for its default is saved at its default again (the save icon, Save as new).

Changes stay on this keyboard, shown as \"Custom 1 · from Sunset\". The saved item changes only with its save icon in the list, which asks which other keyboards using it get the change. Everything waits for the screen\'s Save; Discard undoes it everywhere.
Key edits stay on this keyboard, as for Layouts and themes; the set changes only with its save icon. Saved Layouts holding the set are listed with ticks too.
Edited in the palette editor; Discard there, or on Appearance, undoes it.
Edits the layout file: every keyboard using it changes. Layout & Typing\'s Discard undoes it.
With separate settings, each keyboard\'s settings are its own; with one set of settings, a change reaches every keyboard.
Saves this keyboard\'s settings under a new name. If another saved item has exactly these settings, the dialog says so; it still saves.
Long-press the name. Every keyboard and saved item naming it follows. Waits for the screen\'s Save.
In the palette editor. Keyboards and saved themes naming it follow.
Keyboards and saved Layouts using it follow.
Long-press the keyboard\'s name.
Off the list only. Keyboards using it keep its settings, shown as Custom 1, Custom 2 …; nothing goes back to the default. The dialog names them. Waits for the screen\'s Save.
Off the list. Keyboards using it keep its popups as Custom N; saved Layouts keep its popups without the name, and it never comes back by itself.
Off the list. Keyboards and saved themes using it keep its colours as Custom N. One nothing uses is deleted.
Off the list; keyboards and themes using it keep it. One nothing uses: you\'re asked whether to delete the file for good.
Off the picture list; keyboards and themes keep their copies.
Off the list. Every keyboard using it keeps its keys as an unsaved layout of its own, whether it chose it or had it as the default for that part.
Its learned and blacklisted words go too. Keyboards reading them (\"Use lists from other keyboards\") are named, and one you pick can take them, merged into its own.
Only if no other keyboard has the language; if one does, you can turn the language off on this keyboard instead.
Delete in the Learned list: gone as if never typed, also for keyboards reading this list.
Delete in the Blacklisted list: the word can be suggested again.
Remove (long-press a suggestion) deletes it there too, with the learned word, and blacklists it on this keyboard.
Unpin or delete it in the clipboard: one list for every keyboard.
A setting\'s Default button: this keyboard only. It then follows the latest default.
Choosing the Layout, theme or popup set again brings back what it carries.
Add a palette, or Load one from a file or text.
Load a font file in a text style. The same font loaded again is reused; a font taken off the list comes back.
Pick a picture: it joins the picture list every keyboard chooses from.
Add custom layout (paste one into the editor), or Load file in Full customization with JSON.
Add a keyboard, or a copy of one. A new keyboard can start with words from other keyboards.
Add from Downloads, or get one from curmudgeon.works.
Add word, in Android\'s personal dictionary.
Save the palette to a file, or copy it as text, in the palette editor.
A backup holds everything (Backup and restore).
Included as they are, with the values their unpicked settings had when saved.
Each keyboard\'s settings: only what you picked.
Fonts, pictures, custom key layouts and added dictionaries are included.
Learned and blacklisted words, Android\'s personal dictionary and the clipboard are included.
Choose keyboards: those not on this phone are marked new and ticked; those here start unticked, and restoring one replaces it.

Come in unless one with the same content is here already (then that one is used). A name in use gets the next free number, \"Sunset 2\"; with \"bring them in as copies\" off, it is not brought in, and the restored keyboards that chose it keep its look but name no item: they show \"Custom 1\" (a Layout that held such a popup set keeps its popups and names no set). A Layout\'s popup set is matched first, and the keyboards point at what their items became.

Come in like the saved items: the same file here already is used; a name in use for another file gets the next free number, \"Mine 2\", and the restored keyboards, themes (fonts, pictures) and Layouts (key layouts) name that one. This phone\'s file is never replaced, so its other keyboards keep it.
Added to this phone\'s, never replacing them.
The phone\'s \"Saved items take new defaults\" switch stays as it is.

Wipes this phone\'s settings and replaces everything with the backup\'s: keyboards, saved items, files, word lists, dictionaries and clipboard. The phone\'s \"Saved items take new defaults\" switch stays as it is.
What you picked stays; what you never picked follows the new defaults.

With \"Saved items take new defaults\" on, the keyboards using a saved item take the new defaults for the settings it saved at their default; off, the update changes no keyboard. Built-ins always follow.
Stay as they are.
Stay as they are.
Every setting back to its default. Ticks decide whether keyboards and languages go back too.
Kept, unless \"Your own layouts, popup layouts, saved themes and Layouts …\" is ticked.
Kept, unless ticked (learned words, clipboard history).
On: each keyboard gets a copy of the common settings, then its own (a keyboard that had its own before keeps them).
Off: every keyboard uses one set, from the keyboard you pick; each keyboard\'s own settings stay stored and come back when it\'s on again.
Saved items are shared by all keyboards either way. With one set of settings, the update and delete dialogs have no keyboards to tick.
Each keyboard always keeps its own learned and blacklisted words.
